newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury undecided on commerce and bank reform.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury undecided on commerce and bank reform.

text.p: The Clinton administration, hard at work on a proposal to reform U.S. banking laws, has not reached a decision on the controversial issue of allowing commercial firms to own banks, a top Treasury official said on Friday.

"We're looking at all the different approaches," Undersecretary for Domestic Finance John Hawke said to reporters after a congressional hearing on debt collection. "We haven't settled on any particular appoach."
Under a law passed by Congress last year, the administration was required to submit a report on bank reform by March 31, but the report is still not finished, Hawke said.
"It's a very time consuming process," he said.
The administration's bank reform plan is expected to allow banks to mix with other financial services such as securities firms and insurance companies.
But on the broader question of allowing financial and nonfinancial firms to mix, the administration is still undecided on its approach.
Some in Congress favor allowing unlimited mixing, while others, including House Banking Chairman Jim Leach of Iowa, are completely opposed.
A possible compromise would allow limited combinations. The administration is said to be leaning toward this approach, known as a basket, according to people familiar with the administration's plan.
